target_customer: Large Shopify merchants with high support ticket volume that use Gorgias, Zendesk or Kustomer
problem: Ecommerce brands spend heavily on offshore support staff with high turnover and poor quality, and earlier automation was disappointing.
business_model: Usage-based B2B SaaS, brands pay per ticket fully resolved
product_category: AI customer support agents for ecommerce

founders.name: Guillaume Luccisano
prior_employers: Justin.tv and Twitch (early member, per podcast description)
previous_startups: Triplebyte (S15, co-founder, later acquired per a profile)
founders.background_notes: YC page says Yuma is his third YC startup and that he is a seed investor in 60+ companies.

technical_complexity.rationale: Agent orchestration with integrations into helpdesks and Shopify actions with safety limits was real engineering, but built on third party LLMs.

defensibility.rationale: Deep helpdesk and commerce integrations and tuned processes create some lock in, but the underlying models are shared and the category had many entrants.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Helpdesks added their own AI agents (Gorgias Automate per 2026 comparison articles); Yuma remained active with 140+ brands per its site.

market_need_then: Company says merchants with $10M plus revenue hate support and had been promised automation for years; a prototype released in Dec 2022 drew a flood of demo requests.

branding.community_and_virality: Founder has a podcast interview and customer case studies; no evidence of brand driven virality.

brand_strength.rationale: No sources on the name or identity; brand is functional and the Yuma name is shared with other firms (Yuma AZ, a Bittensor company).

outcome_analysis: Yuma began as a prototype on the Gorgias app store in late 2022 and joined YC W23. It reports 100 plus paying customers and over 1 million tickets resolved by October 2024 and 140 plus brands by 2026, with a team of 26. A $5M round was announced in October 2024 and a prior seed closed in spring 2023. The serial founder with two earlier YC companies, ChatGPT timing and a narrow Shopify wedge helped. Helpdesk incumbents adding their own AI is the main risk.
notes: The company blog says the seed closed in spring 2023 with an additional investment in summer 2024 that lifted valuation to over $30M; no amounts or exact dates for those, so only the $5M announcement (Oct 30, 2024 press release) is recorded and the post money is left null. Geo.sig.ai calls it a $5M Series A led by Sequoia, uncorroborated and not recorded. Aggregators give total raised $5.2M to $5.8M. No dated 2023 competitor sources found; 2026 comparison pages only.
